# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–36 (Updated 2026-10-13, Final Revision)

## Setting and Time
- **Current Period**: Winter of ninth year after Waterloo (1830). Story spans from Sunday, 26th April dinner (Chapters 1–35) through Chapter 36 (winter and spring). Dinner for Emperor of China scheduled Monday, 8th July (three weeks ahead as of Chapter 35). Chapter 36 set in market towns (Bryngate, Mirecombe, Coldcombe, Dunholt, Gulton, Salwick, Staveton) and London (Welbeck Street, Grosvenor Square, Abchurch Lane, Islington, Beargarden Club).
- **Key Locations**: London (Welbeck Street, Grosvenor Square, Abchurch Lane, Beargarden Club, Bruton Street, Queen's Gate, Islington); Coventry Island; Queen's Crawley; rural areas (Sheep's Acre Farm, Staveton).

## Major Deaths
John Sedley, Mr. Osborne, Joseph Sedley, Colonel Rawdon Crawley, Sir Pitt, Wevie Lindner (died winter, buried Salmere).

## Rebecca's Arc
Never became Lady Crawley; styles herself so. Son (Sir Rawdon) receives allowance but refuses to see her. Appears wealthy at Bath/Cheltenham, busies herself with piety and Charity Lists.

## Amelia and William Dobbin
Married at Ostend; Amelia initiated encounter. Dobbin quit service, rented "the Evergreens" (Hampshire). Devoted father; daughter Jane his pride.

## Lady Carbury and Family

**Lady Carbury**: Welbeck Street resident with Felix and Henrietta. Authored "Criminal Queens." Crushed by "Evening Pulpit" review; praised by "Morning Breakfast Table" (Mr. Broune). Chapter 35 (late): Mr. Broune proposed marriage; she rejected via letter by six o'clock evening, sent via Didon to Pall Mall East. Full of regrets; in debt. Chapter 36: Attended soirée with Roger Carbury; returned home to find Paul and Henrietta together. Disbelieved accidental visit claim. Cross-examined Henrietta on intentions. Expressed scorn at Henrietta's suggestion of marrying for railway fortune despite her own efforts for advantageous matches for Felix. Allowed Henrietta to leave after kissing.

**Felix Carbury**: Beautiful; cynosure of mother's eyes. Won £2,000 from Lord Grasslough, £400 from Miles Grendall at gaming. Director of South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway. Chapter 35: Kissed Marie's lips when alone. Made appointment with Ruby Ruggles at kitchen-garden bottom (Sheep's Acre); neglected it. Melmotte offered advancement and £200 cheque if Felix withdrew from Marie. Wrote letter to Ruby excusing himself, claiming summoned to Liverpool on American railway business. Chapter 36: Showed Marie his renunciation letter to her father; lied claiming it was necessary. **Sunday morning (whilst father transacts business with Paul at Grosvenor Square): Met Marie in Grosvenor Square gardens during church time. Marie had key and arranged unlocked gate via Didon. Marie proposed elopement plan: Marie and Didon (as "aunt") travel as French party; Felix as "American" named Smith; board S.S. "Adriatic" (White Star boat) Thursday week at noon from Liverpool; marry at New York or on board; return within month; Didon to receive £50, male assistant £10. All arranged beforehand; Felix merely needs provide funds and confirm within day or two. Felix feels both gratitude and fear: funds tied up with Melmotte, no security to offer Vossner for loans, terrified of elopement immediately after renouncing Marie to her father.**

**Henrietta Carbury**: Rejected Roger's suit (too young, age disparity). Paul returned "as still dear friend" within week, promising not to see her three months. Wore rose from Roger's room. Roger declared love anew (Chapter 32 evening); determination unshaken. Paul thoroughly in love with her. Chapter 36: Paul visited her at Welbeck Street in Lady Carbury's absence. Felt caught when discovered together though innocent. Told mother: "He is so much above me, that, though I do love him, I cannot think of him in that way. And I have told you that I do love some one else." Praised Roger as "rock of strength" who "never lies."

## Ruby Ruggles
Granddaughter of Daniel Ruggles (Sheep's Acre). Pretty with long glossy ringlets. **Chapter 36: Now in London, working as servant/maid to Mrs. Pipkin (her aunt, mother's brother's widow) at Islington who lets lodgings with five children. Mrs. Pipkin quite respectable. Ruby minding children when Paul visited Saturday morning. Paul's visit: Found Mrs. Hurtle out for day. Ruby answered door. Paul felt justice of her reproach—what business had he to be Mentor in affairs of love, having engaged himself to Mrs. Hurtle and having declared love to Hetta previous evening? Ruby cautioned Paul not to speak of her. Mrs. Hurtle gone to Southend for day with Mrs. Pipkin; baby with them. Mrs. Hurtle paying for two. Ruby states she is "looked after" by "one as John Crumb ain't fit to touch"—implying Sir Felix. Paul realized Roger's fear about Felix well founded.**

**John Crumb**: Country lover from Suffolk. Chapter 35: After supper, moved to take Ruby's hand; Ruby fled. Rode to Carbury Hall searching for her. Chapter 36: Had been communicating with Ruby and searching for her. (Described as "Bungay mealman.")

**Daniel Ruggles**: Holds Sheep's Acre Farm on bishop's lease; Roger Carbury's tenant. Chapter 35: Consulted Roger and Father Barham about Ruby's departure. Chapter 36: Has quarrelled with John Crumb; no longer anxious to get back granddaughter. Reconciled to loss.

## The Melmottes

**Augustus Melmotte**: Chairman, South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway Company. Big man with large whiskers; expression of mental power on harsh vulgar face. Rumours of gigantic swindler. Candidate for Westminster parliament seat. Planning Emperor of China dinner (8th July). **Chapter 36 (Sunday morning): Called Paul to Grosvenor Square 11:30 A.M. or afternoon. Melmotte emphasized unanimity essential to Board; without it, nothing achieved; with it, everything. Warned Paul against quarrelling in Board-room, citing risk to widows and children via share depreciation and property annihilation. Credited extended his argument: credit strong as air supporting; fragile as vapour when roughly touched. Offered choice: Paul accept £6,000 and leave Company, or go abroad (stating Paul would be useful, "making of the railway"); promised personal responsibility for payment before year's end. Paul agreed to consider, meet him at Abchurch Lane before next Board day. Melmotte hastened departure, claiming to keep Sir Gregory Gribe (Bank Director) waiting downstairs (though Gribe's presence doubted).**

**Marie Melmotte**: Speaks English well; forming own opinions. Rejected Lord Grasslough. Chapter 35: Engaged to Lord Nidderdale. Refused to give Felix up. Not wedded to Grosvenor Square grandeur. Chapter 36: **Devised elopement plan with Felix: Travel to Liverpool, board S.S. "Adriatic" Thursday week at noon bound for New York. Marry on board or at New York. Return within month to force father's acceptance. Didon to pose as aunt; Felix as American "Smith"; Marie as French girl. Obtained Felix's consent. Marie "certainly a clever girl." Had key to Grosvenor Square gardens; arranged Didon to unlock gate, permit Felix entrance undetected during Sunday church time.**

## The Longestaffes

**Sir Merton Longestaffe**: Determined no London expenses; family will not return from Caversham. Desires to sell Pickering and disembarrass Caversham from debt. Dolly refused consent unless half produce given to him.

**Georgiana Longestaffe**: Made protest against Melmottes. Following morning received invitation to stay with them. By Sunday, present at Grosvenor Square.

**Adolphus (Dolly) Longestaffe**: Has rooms in Bruton Street. States father cannot sell Pickering without his consent.

## South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway Scheme

**The Enterprise**: Railway from Salt Lake City, branching from San Francisco/Chicago line, through New Mexico/Arizona into Mexico, terminating Vera Cruz. Approximately 2,000 miles.

**Financial Strategy**: Stock at par; shares sold at premium "to run them up even to 110," yielding minimum three hundred thousand dollars. Directors understood fortune made by floating shares, not building railway.

**London Directorate**: Melmotte (chairman), Lord Alfred Grendall, Sir Felix Carbury, Samuel Cohenlupe (MP for Staines), Lord Nidderdale, Paul Montague.

## Paul Montague and Mrs. Winifrid Hurtle

**Paul's Situation**: Living at Beargarden. Junior railway firm member. Dislikes Fisker. Trembles for his money. Thoroughly in love with Hetta. **Chapter 36: Returned from Liverpool Friday morning. Resolved to tell Mrs. Hurtle face-to-face he would not marry her due to dissatisfaction with her past. After Board, joined Nidderdale at Beargarden. Visited Hetta at Welbeck Street; claimed accidental visit. Walked with Roger to his hotel. Confided Mrs. Hurtle in London; been with her three or four times. Told Roger all—rumoured duel, rumoured murder, rumour of existing husband. Declared: "But even if the rumours be untrue I will not marry her." Roger urged him to cheat "Devil" if bargain made. Both resolved Paul should visit Islington next morning, tell Mrs. Hurtle all stories heard, declare resolution never to marry. Saturday morning, 9 A.M.: Paul took Hansom cab to Islington; found Mrs. Hurtle out for day. Ruby answered. Paul wrote note in pencil: came immediately on return from Liverpool, sorry she away. When should he call again? Note postponed confrontation. Evening: Mrs. Hurtle returned from Southend. Sent note: "I am so sorry to have been away. I will expect you all to-morrow. W. H." Sunday morning: breakfasted late, walked to Grosvenor Square to meet Melmotte. Pondered what Melmotte would say; understood war declared. Prepared go to wall regarding money, hoping save character and honest reputation. Intended ask Mr. Ramsbottom draw statement for publication.**

**Mrs. Winifrid Hurtle**: Formerly betrothed to Paul. Arrived Wednesday. During earlier engagement promised to follow him; renewed promises in New York. Theatre evening: Paul took her. After theatre, declined cab but Paul accompanied. Does not like Frenchmen; prefers Englishmen to Americans. Thinks he should marry her or world hear story of his perjury. **Chapter 36: Out for day with Mrs. Pipkin and baby to Southend. Returning evening. Sent note to Paul after return: "I am so sorry to have been away. I will expect you all to-morrow. W. H." Most fond of baby, like Mrs. Pipkin.**

## Lord Nidderdale
Intent on marrying Marie for fortune. Chapter 35: Marie engaged to Nidderdale. Chapter 36: At Beargarden with Paul.

## Mr. Broune
Editor, "Morning Breakfast Table." Nearer fifty than sixty; young of his age. Chapter 35 (late evening): Proposed to Lady Carbury. When he read her rejection letter: stood at fireplace, left letter on table. Felt admiration greater than ever.

## Roger Carbury
Nearly forty. Never owed shilling he couldn't pay. Firmly opposed Melmotte connection on principle. Works as priest on day-labourer's wages. Soft heart; knows Lady Carbury false and Felix worthless. Declared love to Henrietta anew (Chapter 32 evening); determination unshaken. Chapter 36: Attended soirée with Lady Carbury. Found Paul and Henrietta together. Walked with Paul to his hotel; confirmed fears regarding Felix and Ruby well founded.

## Other Characters
- **Miles Grendall**: Secretary to Melmotte. Does not pay debts of honour.
- **Father John Barham**: Priest, Beccles.
- **Mr. Ramsbottom**: Liverpool gentleman. Paul resolved ask him draw statement for publication re: Company.
- **Mrs. Pipkin**: Ruby's aunt (mother's brother's widow). Quite respectable; lets lodgings with five children.
- **Sir Gregory Gribe**: Bank Director; claimed by Melmotte to be waiting at Grosvenor Square (presence doubted).
- **Didon**: Marie's attendant; facilitates elopement plan; to receive £50 before boarding ship.
